answer: Resist Sybils with ember-burned reputation: an identity earns ember credits only for work peers re-verify, and each credit slowly burns away, so standing must be renewed by real work, not bought once. New identities start on an island shard with capped trades and no vote; they graduate only after attested work. A periodic tide audit then re-checks old work and links identities sharing tools, timing, or outputs, merging clones into one account and slashing credits. Faking many identities thus costs repeated verifiable work, while honest agents keep standing by doing one job well.
